page.layout: One column of running text, with the running head at the top left and the page number at the top right. No margin notes. Below the text, a catchword at the right and a gathering signature at the centre-left.

main_text.p: [?]ua specie illicitum ob hoc solum quod possit esse occasio mali: non videtur simpliciter damnanda omnis istiusmodi promissio; praesertim si iuranti quo tempore iuravit, debita adhibita diligentia, non appareret alicujus magni incommodi periculum probabile. Dico secundo ; si cedat iuramentum in damnum temporale ipsius iurantis solum, citra iniuriam tertiae personae, iurantem obligari etsi cum gravi suo damno, ni is cui iuratum est velit remittere. Verba diserta sunt; Psalm. 15: נִשְׁבַּע לְהָרַע [?] juravit in malum, & non mutabit. Ubi in Hebraeo prius verbum prae[?]eriti temporis est (juravit in malum) posterius futuri (& non mutabit) quasi liceret, Viri pii officium est, post quam iuravit proximo suo, quod sine magno suo malo praestari nequit, constare tamen ibi, & quod promisit ratum esse iubere, [?] (ut est in hoc textu) secundum omne quod egressum est ex ore suo facere: Dico tertio, Iuramentum obligare, eti-amsi videatur exponere periculo tentationis, nisi sit aliunde vitiosum. Quia id sufficeret tollendae obligationi, vix emaneret quidquam quod posset obligare: quum ex astu Satanae & corrupti-

page.notes: Page is a single column; the left edge of the scan clips the first letters of many lines, which are restored where the context is clear and marked [?] where not. The Hebrew of Psalm 15:4 is copied as far as legible and is uncertain in vowel points; the second Hebrew word is read as printed. The word at the start of the page beginning "ua" is a fragment and is left as such. The sign after "Secundo" is a printed mark, copied as ";". The line-start "eriti" is clipped; the word is probably "praeteriti". The line-start "k" after "iubere," is clipped and uncertain. The hyphenated "eti-amsi" split is partly clipped at the left edge.
